title: Analytical tests to evaluate pozzolanic reaction in lime stabilized soils
author: Akula, Little
materials: Differential thermogravimteric analysis (DTA) is a widely applied technique to measure hydration and carbonation by cement scientists. The DTA analysis results of the treated and untreated samples are shown in Fig. 3. In this study, DTA was used to identify pozzolanic products such as C-S-H. The temperature region from 0°C to 140°C can be attributed to moisture loss. Similar observations were made by Al-Mukhthar [13] for lime treated samples. In the treated sample, Ca2+ absorption on the net negative surfaces of smectite can affect moisture content. The difference in peak height between the treated and untreated samples at 100°C also indicated that the treated sample contained less moisture as compared to the untreated sample. Karen [30] showed that the temperature region for C-S-H occupies a wide area between 0°C to 300°C for hydrated cement pastes. The temperature region between 140°C and 240°C has been used to identify the formation of C-S-H in the treated soil. The treated samples S1 and S2 show a higher peak in the 140°C to 240°C region when compared with the untreated sample indicating the presence of C-S-H. In addition, the calcite (C) peak at 640°C to 700°C indicates carbonation reactions. Peaks from soil minerals such as smectite and kaolinite are seen in the region 400°C to 600°C [41, 42].Fig. 3Differential thermogravimteric analysis plots of samples S1 (left) and S2 (right).Figure 3

steps.title: Collect representative soil sample
steps.instruction: Recover a 5 g representative sample from each of the treated and untreated specimens.

steps.title: Air‑dry sample
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the collected sample for 72 h; if grinding difficulty occurs, extend the drying period by an additional 24 h.

steps.title: Grind sample to fine powder
steps.instruction: Grind the air‑dried sample with a mortar and pestle until the material passes a No. 325 (0.44 mm) sieve, breaking agglomerated clay particles.

steps.title: Back‑load XRD sample holder
steps.instruction: Back‑load the ground powder onto the XRD sample holder to reduce preferred orientation caused by stacking of clay minerals.

steps.title: Acquire XRD diffraction pattern
steps.instruction: Run the XRD scan from 50 to 700 2θ using a 26 mm diameter powder sample, spinning at 15 rpm, with a scan rate of 0.70 2θ/min; total measurement time ≈45.5 min.

steps.title: Moisture‑equilibrate samples for DTA
steps.instruction: Place both treated and untreated ground samples in a desiccator containing CaSO₄ as desiccant and equilibrate for 14 days.

steps.title: Perform DTA analysis
steps.instruction: Immediately after equilibration, analyze each sample (minimum 50 mg) in an alumina DTA holder; heat from 40 °C to 1000 °C at 200 °C/min under nitrogen purge at 30 mL/min; total run time 90 min.
